Cooking & recipes 2

Cook real Thai dishes and balance their flavours — curries, soups, and getting the seasoning right. This second part goes beyond technique into the dishes themselves: the ตะไคร้ (lemongrass) and ใบมะกรูด (kaffir lime leaves) behind ต้มยำ (tom yum), adding กะทิ (coconut milk) late so it doesn't split, and frying the เครื่องแกง (curry paste) first. It covers heat control — ไฟอ่อน (low heat) versus ไฟแรง (high heat) — and chasing a กลมกล่อม (well-balanced) taste. All 27 sentences come with native-speed audio, English translations, and word-by-word notes, so the recipe language sinks in by ear.

1 ตะไคร้…
ทำต้มยำต้องมีตะไคร้กับใบมะกรูดนะ
To make tom yum you need lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves.
ทำ=makeต้มยำ=tom yumต้องมี=you needตะไคร้=lemongrassกับ=andใบมะกรูด=kaffir lime leavesนะ=softening particle
ต้มยำ (hot-and-sour soup) gets its aroma from fresh ตะไคร้ (lemongrass), ข่า (galangal) and ใบมะกรูด (kaffir lime leaves). These are infused for fragrance and pushed aside, not eaten.
2 กะทิ…

ใส่=addกะทิ=coconut milkตอนท้ายๆ=near the endจะได้ไม่=so it won'tแตกมัน=curdle
กะทิ (coconut milk) is added late and never boiled hard, so it doesn't แตกมัน — literally 'the oil breaks', i.e. curdles and separates. A real curry-making term.

17 กลมกล่อม…

แกงเขียวหวาน ('green sweet curry') is named for its green colour, from green chillies — not for being sweet. กลมกล่อม describes a rounded, well-balanced flavour.

โจ๊ก is rice boiled until the grains fully disintegrate into a smooth porridge — a standard Thai breakfast, distinct from ข้าวต้ม, where the grains stay whole in a thin soup.
